diagnostic_evidence.quote: the notion of a $(0,\bse,d)$-sequence in base $b$ is identical to that of an equidistributed sequence in base $(b^{e_1}, \dots, b^{e_d})$.

issues.failure_explanation: Both net definitions require every elementary interval with weighted digit sum at most m-t to contain exactly b^t points. Taking all k_j=0, the whole cube must then contain exactly b^t points, but it contains b^m; so for m>t no point set satisfies the definitions, no (t,d)- or (t,e,d)-sequence exists as defined, and the asserted identity between (0,e,d)-sequences and equidistributed sequences (as well as the cited Theorems thm:t-val-nied and thm:added-1) cannot hold for the literal definitions. The intended definition uses equality (or the count b^{m-\sum e_j k_j}).

failure_location.quote: every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $(b^{e_1},\dots,b^{e_d})$ with $e_1k_1 + \cdots + e_dk_d \le m-t$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace '\le m-t' by '= m-t' (or require b^{m-\sum e_j k_j} points) in both net definitions; the equivalence claim and all later results then hold unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The central notion on which the paper's structure-preservation claim rests is mis-defined; the equivalence with equidistributed sequences and the specialisation of all Section 3 results to (0,e,d)-sequences rely on the corrected definition.
issues.title: Definitions of (t,m,d)- and (t,e,m,d)-nets are vacuous as written ("<= m-t" with "exactly b^t points")
issues.why_classification: A local, standard correction to the definitions restores every claim without altering any argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: L_{\bsl} = \{ \bsh = (h_1,\dots,h_d) \in \NN_0^d \mid b^{l_j-1} \le h_j < b^{l_j} \text{ if } l_j>0, \text{ and } h_j=0 \text{ if } l_j=0 \}.
covers exactly the set of all Walsh indices $\bsh$ where $h_j < b^{k_j+1}$ for all $j \in u$ and $h_j=0$ for $j \notin u$.

Then, by inclusion-exclusion principle, \eqref{eq:beta2}, 
the above equation, and Eq.~\eqref{eq:beta},

issues.failure_explanation: For l_j=k'_j+1>=1 the set L_l requires b^{k'_j} <= h_j, so h_j>=1. The union over k'<=k therefore covers only indices with 1<=h_j<b^{k_j+1} for j in u, not all h_j<b^{k_j+1}; the appendix's covering claim is false. Hence sum_{k'<=k} beta_{u,k'} equals tilde beta_{u,u,k} minus all Walsh terms with some h_j=0 (j in u); e.g. in one dimension it equals tilde beta_{u,u,k} - f_emptyset. The correct identity is sum_{k'<=k} beta_{u,k'} = sum_{v subseteq u} (-1)^{|u|-|v|} tilde beta_{v,v,k_v}. The proof of Lemma lem:beta-basechange invokes (eq:beta2) to rewrite sum_{l_j<L_j} beta^U_{u,l} as tilde beta^U_{u,u,L-1}, which is false term by term; the lemma's conclusion nevertheless holds because the omitted h_j=0 terms cancel in the alternating sum over v, but this is not argued.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace (eq:beta2) by the inclusion–exclusion identity over subsets v of u (or by the Walsh characterisation with 1<=h_j<b^{k_j+1}), correct the appendix covering claim, and in Lemma lem:beta-basechange note that the extra h_j=0 terms cancel under the alternating sum over v.
issues.overall_effect: Displayed identity (eq:beta2) and its appendix proof are wrong; the proof of Lemma lem:beta-basechange (and thus the justification of (eq:sigma_basechange) used in Section 4) is invalid as written, although the lemma's statement is true.
issues.title: Identity (eq:beta2) is false: the sum of ANOVA components omits the terms with some h_j=0; appendix proof and Lemma lem:beta-basechange's proof rely on it
issues.why_classification: The lemma's conclusion and all downstream comparisons survive; the fix is a short local correction of the identity and a routine cancellation observation.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Since $C_{u,v,k}(n) = n$ holds for this value of $n$, the original proof applies directly.

issues.failure_explanation: With C defined with the factor 1/n^2 (eq:C_def), the count t(q+1)^2+(m-t)q^2 of pairs in common intervals is n^2 C, not C, so (eq:Cformula) and the claim C=n for n<=m_{u,\emptyset,k} are false by a factor n^2. Likewise, expanding the product in (eq:Gtilda_def) gives \tilde G = n \sum_v H_{u,v} C with the stated normalisations, contradicting (eq:Gtilda_formula). Only the un-normalised counts (no 1/n, no 1/n^2) make (eq:G_Gtilde), (eq:Gtilda_formula), (eq:Cformula) and G=1 for n<=m_{u,\emptyset,k} mutually consistent; the paper's later computations (Theorem thm:mimic(iii), Corollary cor:maxgain_uk) silently use the un-normalised version.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the factor 1/n from (eq:Gtilda_def) and 1/n^2 from (eq:C_def) (or equivalently move the factors into (eq:G_Gtilde) and (eq:Gtilda_formula)); all subsequent statements then hold verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: As literally stated, (eq:Cformula), (eq:Gtilda_formula) and item (i) of Theorem thm:mimic are false under Definition def:gain; the intended results hold once the normalisation is made consistent.
issues.title: Normalisation of \tilde G and C in Definition def:gain is inconsistent with (eq:Gtilda_formula), Lemma lem:Cformula and Theorem thm:mimic
issues.why_classification: A consistent renormalisation of two definitions restores every result; no argument changes.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
If $n = r m_{u,u,\bsk}$ for $r \in \NN$, then
\[
G_{u,\bsk}(n) = 0.
\]

issues.failure_explanation: From (eq:Cformula), C_{u,v,k'}(b_j n) = b_j C_{u,v,k}(n), which yields G_{u,k'}(n b_j) = G_{u,k}(n) (index k on the right), not G_{u,k'}(n). Counterexample to (iv) as written: u={1}, b_1=2, k'=1, n=2: G_{{1},1}(4)=0 by (ii) while G_{{1},1}(2)=1 by (i). Iterating the correct (iv) gives G_{u,k}(n \prod_j b_j^{k_j}) = G_{u,0}(n), not with \prod_j b_j; counterexample to (v) as written: u={1}, b_1=2, k=2, n=2: G_{{1},2}(4)=1 by (i) but G_{{1},0}(2)=0 by (ii).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (iv) as G_{u,k'}(n b_j) = G_{u,k}(n) and (v) as G_{u,k}(n \prod_{j\in u} b_j^{k_j}) = G_{u,0}(n).
issues.overall_effect: Items (iv) and (v) of Theorem thm:mimic are false as stated; items (vii), Corollary cor:gain-0ed and cor:maxgain_uk depend only on the correct scaling relations (as in the cited source) and remain valid.
issues.title: Theorem thm:mimic items (iv) and (v) are misstated (wrong index/exponent) and false as written
issues.why_classification: Correcting the indices restores the intended (and cited) statements; no downstream result is affected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\tilde{P}_n$ be its randomly scrambled version using a nested scramble with two-fold uniformity.
obtained by a random scrambling of $\Scal$ in base $\bsb$ that ensures two-fold uniformity.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is derived from (eq:variance-gain), which Theorem thm:added-2 states only for nested scrambles with two-fold uniformity. The corollary (unlike Corollary cor:added-1) imposes no uniformity condition; for a nested scramble lacking two-fold uniformity (e.g. a random digit shift in base b^{e_j}, which is nested and one-fold uniform), the variance is not given by (eq:variance-gain) and the stated bound is unsupported.

failure_location.quote: let $\tilde{\bsx}_0, \tilde{\bsx}_1, \tilde{\bsx}_2, \dots$ be a randomly scrambled version of $\Scal$ in base $\bsb=(b^{e_1}, \dots, b^{e_d})$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add 'nested scramble with two-fold uniformity' to the hypotheses of Corollary cor:added-2 (and to the standing assumptions of Section 4).
issues.overall_effect: As stated, the variance bound for coarse scrambling lacks a needed hypothesis; the same omission affects the Section 4 variance comparisons that rely on (eq:variance-gain).
issues.title: Corollary cor:added-2 omits the two-fold uniformity hypothesis required by the variance formula it invokes
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypothesis already used elsewhere in the paper fully restores the result.
